stories.headline: Ebola has tortured us: Fear grips eastern DR Congo as deadly virus spreads
stories.summary: Ebola has spread in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, causing fear among residents as the suspected number of deaths rises. The outbreak, first detected on April 24, may have been circulating undetected earlier, according to Congolese Health Minister Dr. Samuel Roger Kamba. After visiting Ituri province, the epicenter of the outbreak, Kamba acknowledged that health teams are struggling to catch up with the virus. The Ebola strain spreading in Congo and Uganda has no approved vaccine. Ebola is a deadly viral disease spread through direct contact with bodily fluids, causing severe bleeding and organ failure. First identified in 1976, it is believed to have originated in bats. Health officials are working to contain the outbreak, but the lack of a vaccine and potential earlier circulation of the virus pose significant challenges. The situation remains dire, with the number of suspected deaths continuing to rise.

stories.headline: Takes two to Tango: JD Vance on US-Iran peace talks, says ‘good progress’ made; military action is ‘option B’
stories.summary: US Vice President JD Vance stated that "good progress" has been made in US-Iran peace talks, with negotiations being pursued in good faith. Tehran appears willing to deal, according to Vance. However, he warned that if a deal is not agreed to, the US will explore "a lot of options," with military action being "option B." Vance said the US could restart the military campaign if necessary. Despite this, he expressed optimism about the current state of negotiations, saying they are in a "pretty good spot." The Vice President urged Iran to "take the next step" towards peace, implying that the US is waiting for Tehran to make further concessions to reach an agreement. Vance's comments suggest that while the US prefers a diplomatic solution, it is prepared to consider other options if talks fail.

stories.headline: San Diego mosque shooting reflects how online rhetoric, media depictions and political discourse contribute to increased Islamophobia
stories.summary: A shooting at the Islamic Center of San Diego has left three worshipers dead, deepening fear among the Muslim American community. The suspected shooters, who killed themselves after the attack, had hate speech and anti-Islamic writing in their vehicle, according to investigators. The incident reflects a rise in Islamophobia, fueled by negative online rhetoric, media depictions, and political discourse. Muslim Americans are experiencing increased discrimination, hate crimes, and psychological harm due to these portrayals. The San Diego mosque shooting has heightened feelings of vulnerability and powerlessness among the community. The attack is being investigated, with authorities examining the role of hate speech and anti-Islamic ideology in motivating the shooters. The incident has sparked concerns about the consequences of perpetuating negative stereotypes and rhetoric against Muslims.

stories.headline: Africa launches negotiators academy to fix bad mining, debt and trade deals
stories.summary: Africa has launched the Sankoree Institute of Global Negotiators (SIGN), a program aimed at training government officials and technical experts to negotiate better international agreements. The initiative was unveiled in Kigali, Rwanda, during the Africa CEO Forum, and is endorsed by four Heads of State. SIGN will focus on improving negotiation skills in areas such as mining, debt, trade, health, and climate finance. The academy is led by ex-presidents and is part of the Accra Reset sovereignty agenda. The goal is to strengthen Africa's capacity to secure favorable outcomes in major international agreements, addressing issues such as bad mining and debt deals. The program is a first-of-its-kind credentialing initiative, marking a significant step towards enhancing Africa's negotiation capabilities.

stories.headline: Kotaku] Kickstarter Reverses Controversial NSFW Ban And Blames Stripe Kickstarter's COO stated that the now-reverted NSFW guidelines were put in place due to campaigns being 'suspended by Stripe mid-funding'
stories.summary: Kickstarter has reversed its recent ban on NSFW content, reinstating its previous guidelines. The company's COO stated that the now-reverted guidelines were introduced due to campaigns being suspended by payment processor Stripe mid-funding. Stripe's requirements, driven by its own legal considerations, primarily drove the updates to Kickstarter's mature content rules. The reversal comes just over a week after the introduction of the controversial updates, which prohibited several forms of NSFW content. The change had caused concern among comic creators who rely on the platform to fund their work. With the reversal, Kickstarter's content guidelines have returned to their previous state, allowing creators to post and fundraise for mature content without the recently introduced restrictions. The move is seen as a response to backlash from the community and a effort to accommodate creators' needs.

stories.headline: [9to5Google] Google announces Wear OS 7 with Live Updates, widgets, more A significant lineup of changes is coming to Pixel Watches with Wear OS 7, as Google announces the new wearable
stories.summary: Google has announced Wear OS 7, a major update to its wearable operating system, which will bring significant changes to Pixel Watches and other supported smartwatches. The new version will feature improved battery life, with up to 10% better performance for devices upgrading from Wear OS 6. Wear OS 7 will also introduce new AI-powered experiences, enhanced widgets, and updated notifications and media controls. The update is set to release later this year, but developers can try it out now through the Canary channel. The changes aim to align Wear OS more closely with Android's design, providing a fresh and updated user experience. Wear OS 7 promises to make smartwatch apps feel more connected and will be available on supported devices later this year.

stories.headline: [The Verge] Kickstarter just killed its new mature content rules “Honestly? We botched it.”
stories.summary: Kickstarter has retracted its new mature content rules, admitting they "botched it." The rules, introduced last week, were intended to provide detailed guidelines for adult-oriented content on the platform. However, the community responded negatively, letting Kickstarter know "loud and clear" that they got it wrong. As a result, Kickstarter is going back to the drawing board to reassess its approach. The company is also pushing Stripe, its payment processor, for more flexibility, clarity, and consistency in its policies. Kickstarter's goal was to provide clear guidelines for creators, but the new rules ultimately missed the mark, prompting a swift reversal. The platform will now revisit its approach to mature content, seeking to find a better solution that works for its community.

stories.headline: [9to5Google] Google TV update will support Wii-like pointer remotes At Google I/O 2026, a new focus on pointer remotes – like a Wii remote – is being announced for
stories.summary: At Google I/O 2026, Google announced support for pointer remotes on Google TV, similar to the Wii remote. The update will allow for motion-controlled navigation, making it easier to browse content-heavy pages, including the Google TV home page. Future Google TV devices will increasingly support pointer remotes, bringing cursor-based navigation to televisions. The goal is to improve the user experience and make navigation faster. Developers are being encouraged to update their apps to support the new feature, with official documentation available for implementation details, such as adapting user interfaces and configuring manifest files. The update is part of broader announcements at Google I/O 2026, aiming to change how consumers interact with their Google TV-powered devices.

stories.headline: RR vs LSG Highlights, IPL 2026: Sooryavanshi's 93 helps Rajasthan Royals beat Lucknow Super Giants
stories.summary: Rajasthan Royals beat Lucknow Super Giants by 7 wickets in the IPL 2026. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 93 runs off 38 balls, while Dhruv Jurel contributed an unbeaten 53. The Royals chased down a target of 221, achieving the win in 19.1 overs and finishing at 225 for 3. This victory propelled Rajasthan Royals to fourth place in the IPL 2026 points table. Sooryavanshi's explosive 93 and Jurel's quick innings were key to the team's success, securing a convincing 7-wicket win over the Lucknow Super Giants. The Royals' strong performance helped them climb the rankings, with Sooryavanshi's 93 being a standout performance in the match.

stories.headline: ‘Very natural’ - How Portugal will manage Cristiano Ronaldo at 2026 World Cup as Roberto Martinez admits international methods are different to club coaching
stories.summary: Portugal's manager Roberto Martinez has outlined the team's approach to managing Cristiano Ronaldo at the 2026 World Cup. Martinez stated that traditional club metrics will not apply in the tournament, and the team will focus on day-to-day management. He emphasized that managing players in a World Cup is different from club coaching, and the team will not follow a pattern that fits the club or the player's age. Martinez described managing as "something very natural," indicating a flexible approach. Portugal is expected to adopt a more collective playstyle, moving away from dependence on a single player. The 2026 World Cup is likely to be Ronaldo's final appearance on the world stage, and Martinez's approach aims to get the best out of the team and the legendary forward. The team's strategy will prioritize adaptability and focus.

stories.headline: All-out attack for Tahuhu as retirement fades into background World Cup last-chance a fleeting thought as big picture takes over for White Ferns seamer
stories.summary: New Zealand White Ferns seamer Lea Tahuhu is focusing on an all-out attack as her retirement approaches. The upcoming World Cup is a last-chance opportunity, but Tahuhu's thoughts are on the bigger picture. Recent bowling performances have left her confident that New Zealand will be well-equipped for the future. The team's pace bowling attack is competitive, with multiple players vying for spots in the starting lineup. This depth is seen as a positive sign for the team's prospects. Tahuhu's retirement is looming, but her attention is on the present and ensuring the team's success beyond her departure. The White Ferns are preparing for the World Cup, and Tahuhu's experience will be valuable in the tournament.

stories.headline: The Cleveland Cavs take on the New York Knicks for ECF starting on Tuesday, May 19: Here's how to find, shop, and buy last-minute tickets online.
stories.summary: The Cleveland Cavaliers are set to face the New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference Finals, starting on Tuesday, May 19. This marks the Cavaliers' first trip to the Eastern Conference Finals since 2018, with NBA Finals hopes on the line. The series will determine which team advances to the NBA Finals. Fans can check the Cleveland Cavaliers schedule for game times and opponents, as well as where to watch or listen to radio broadcasts. For those looking to attend games in person, last-minute tickets are available online through ticket hubs like SeatGeek, which offers 100% verified tickets. The platform allows users to browse other dates, venues, and schedules for the series, increasing their chances of finding the right tickets at the right price. Game 1 is scheduled to take place on Tuesday.

stories.headline: PM Modi arrives in Rome for final leg of five-nation tour; meeting with Italian PM Meloni, bilateral cooperation on agenda
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Rome on Tuesday for the final leg of his five-nation tour. He will meet Italian President Sergio Mattarella and hold bilateral discussions with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. The visit aims to boost India-Italy cooperation, with a series of diplomatic engagements scheduled before his return to India on Wednesday. Modi's five-nation tour has taken him to the UAE, the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway, and now Italy. In Norway, he attended the India-Nordic Summit in Oslo and held bilateral meetings with leaders of Norway, Iceland, Finland, and Denmark, stressing deeper cooperation in areas such as trade and innovation. The Rome visit marks the conclusion of his diplomatic tour, with a focus on strengthening ties with Italy.

stories.headline: Commitment to democracy makes India, Nordic nations natural partners: Modi
stories.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that the country's shared commitment to democracy, rule of law, and multilateralism makes India and Nordic nations natural partners. He made this statement at the India-Nordic summit, highlighting the growing strategic partnership between India and the Nordic countries. The partnership is built on shared democratic values and the rule of law. Modi emphasized that converging priorities in areas such as innovation, climate change, and trade have brought the countries closer together. The summit underscores India's keen interest in strengthening ties with the Nordic nations, with high-level interactions taking place since October 2025. The meeting included a joint press conference with leaders from the Nordic countries, where Modi reiterated the importance of mutual commitment to democracy and multilateralism.

stories.headline: CBI arrests Army Ordnance Corps colonel in Kolkata in ₹50 lakh bribery case
stories.summary: Colonel Himanshu Bali, a Colonel-rank officer with the Army Ordnance Corps, was arrested by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in Kolkata for allegedly taking bribes. The CBI registered an FIR against Bali, accusing him of corrupt practices to favour a Kanpur-based private defence supplier. According to the FIR, Bali and Akshat Agrawal, the supplier, met outside official working hours to finalize illicit terms. The bribery amount is reported to be ₹50 lakh. The CBI has recovered over ₹2 crore in the case, which is part of a larger bribery racket in the defence department. Bali's arrest is a result of the CBI's investigation into the racket, which involved misusing official position for personal gain. The case is ongoing, with further investigations being conducted by the CBI.

stories.headline: Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO) has successfully completed the final launched precision guided missile
stories.summary: The Defence Research & Development Organisation (DRDO) has successfully completed trials of the UAV-launched precision guided missile, ULPGM-V3. The trials were conducted at a DRDO test range near Kurnool in Andhra Pradesh using an integrated ground control system (GCS). The ULPGM-V3 is a next-generation weapon developed by DRDO and NewSpace Research and Technologies, enhancing India's drone strike capabilities. The tests were carried out to evaluate the missile's precision guidance and effectiveness. The successful completion of the trials marks a significant boost to India's defence capabilities. The ULPGM-V3 is designed to be launched from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), providing the Indian military with advanced precision strike capabilities. The development and testing of the ULPGM-V3 demonstrate India's progress in developing indigenous defence technologies.

stories.headline: Russian President Vladimir Putin To Visit India For BRICS Summit In September
stories.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin will visit New Delhi in September to attend the BRICS Summit, scheduled for September 12 and 13. The summit will bring together leaders of major emerging economies to discuss global security, economic cooperation, and a multipolar world order. This will be Putin's second trip to India within a year, following his visit in December for the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit. The Kremlin confirmed the visit, which reflects the deepening strategic and defence ties between Moscow and New Delhi. The BRICS Summit is expected to focus on key global issues, and Putin's participation underscores the importance of the event and Russia's relationship with India. The visit is significant, given the current global landscape and the strengthening of ties between the two nations. Putin's attendance was confirmed by Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov.

stories.headline: India-Nordic summit: Why is Modi wooing Northern Europe?
stories.summary: India and the five Nordic countries - Norway, Sweden, Finland, Iceland, and Denmark - are holding a top-level summit in Oslo to strengthen strategic and trade ties. The third India-Nordic summit aims to boost trade, technology, and renewable energy partnerships. Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the summit, marking the first Indian prime ministerial visit to Norway in 43 years. The meeting follows recent trade agreements between India and the European Union, as well as a trade and economic partnership agreement with Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland. The summit's agenda includes increasing business ties, investments, and technology partnerships, and addressing global and economic issues. The India-Nordic ties have been elevated to a Green Technology and Innovation Strategic Partnership, indicating a strong focus on sustainable development and innovation.

stories.headline: UK labour market loses momentum in first quarter as geopolitics start to bite
stories.summary: The UK labour market has lost momentum in the first quarter, despite the IMF upgrading the UK growth forecast. The economic inactivity rate for people aged 16 to 64 years increased to 21.0% in December 2025 to February 2026. The jobs market took a sharp turn for the worse, with payrolled employees falling by 100,000 in April, the biggest single-month drop. Pay growth came in at a slower rate than expected, complicating the labour market response. The decline in the labour market is attributed to geopolitics, with the Northern Ireland effect being a contributing factor. The UK's economic growth has been healthy, but the labour market slide suggests a potential slowdown. The FTSE 100 edged higher, finishing up 6 points at 10,330, despite US stocks coming under pressure. The labour market response has been sharper than expected.

stories.headline: Moneycontrol Pro Panorama | Slow-burn war, enduring pain
stories.summary: Bond markets are experiencing tightening due to persistent inflation pressures. Private credit is supporting India's evolving real estate financing. The 10-year bond yield in India has eased after the second fuel price hike in a week. Global energy prices have been driven up by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. The conflict in Iran has led to prolonged risks, with Fed futures pricing in these risks. The Reserve Bank of India has made a move to curb forex arbitrage, raising concerns. The Indian household is expected to bear the cost of the war decision, with rising energy prices contributing to inflation pressures. The situation is being closely monitored, with bond markets and private credit playing a crucial role in India's economic landscape. Inflation pressures remain a key concern.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty down: Why is stock market falling today? The BSE Sensex fell 389.19 points, or 0.52%, to 74,811.66 in early trade, while the NSE Nifty50 dropped 107.90 points, or 0.46%, to 23,510.10 as of 9:39 am.
stories.summary: The BSE Sensex fell 389.19 points to 74,811.66, a 0.52% decline, in early trade, while the NSE Nifty50 dropped 107.90 points to 23,510.10, a 0.46% decrease, as of 9:39 am. Later, the Nifty50 went below 23,500, and the BSE Sensex was down over 600 points, with Nifty50 trading at 23,421.65, down 196 points or 0.83%, and BSE Sensex at 74,589.42, down 611 points or 0.81%. This decline follows a trend of market volatility, with the Sensex and Nifty50 ending in red on Tuesday. Market analysts expect the market to remain heavily influenced by ongoing events, with elevated volatility in the near term. The benchmark indices have been experiencing significant fluctuations, with the Sensex plunging 939.10 points and Nifty50 falling 284 points in recent trade.

stories.headline: Stock markets open in red, Sensex tank over 500 pts, Nifty down to 23K Indian benchmark equity indices, the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty, experienced a significant drop in early trade due to elevated oil prices, weak global market tren
stories.summary: Indian stock markets opened in the red, with the BSE Sensex tanking over 500 points and the NSE Nifty falling to 23,000. Elevated oil prices and weak global market trends are contributing to the decline. Crude oil prices have surged past $110 per barrel, with Brent crude advancing nearly 2% to trade around $111 per barrel. Renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, particularly concerning Iran, are also weighing on investor sentiment. The rupee is expected to trade in a range of 95.55-96.25. Global markets are witnessing a sharp selloff, with the Nifty slipping below its 50-day Simple Moving Average of 24,000. Analysts predict further selling pressure if the opening zone is not held, with potential targets at 23,400-23,350. The decline is a continuation of the trend seen in recent days, with the Sensex and Nifty experiencing significant drops.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty end lower as banking drag offsets IT rally; rupee hits record low The S&P BSE Sensex slipped 114.19 points, or 0.15%, to close at 75,200.85, while the NSE Nifty50 fell 31.95 points, or 0.14%, to settle at 23,618.
stories.summary: The S&P BSE Sensex fell 114.19 points to 75,200.85, while the NSE Nifty50 declined 31.95 points to 23,618. The Indian stock market indices ended lower due to a drag in the banking sector, which offset gains in the IT sector. The rupee hit a record low for the sixth consecutive session, raising concerns about inflation and the economy. This decline came amid surging crude oil prices, which also contributed to market worries. The Sensex and Nifty's marginal decline reflects the current market sentiment, influenced by external factors such as crude oil prices and the rupee's value. The record low rupee and rising crude oil prices have sparked concerns about the country's economic outlook and inflation rates.

stories.headline: Stock market today: Sensex falls 114 points, Nifty 50 ends at 23,618; mid, small-caps outperform Stock market today: The Sensex lost 114 points, or 0.15%, to close at 75,200.85, while the Nifty 50 ended at 23,618, down 32 points, or 0.14%.
stories.summary: The Sensex fell 114 points, or 0.15%, to close at 75,200.85, while the Nifty 50 ended at 23,618, down 32 points, or 0.14%. Despite the decline in frontline indices, mid and small-cap segments outperformed. The Nifty Bank index dropped 128 points to 53,409, losing over 355 points from the day's highs, indicating continued pressure on financial sectors. IT stocks gained, but the market was pressured by currency concerns and high crude prices, leading to a late sell-off. The decline in the Sensex and Nifty 50 was relatively modest, with the Nifty 50 initially edging higher before closing lower. Broader markets showed resilience, with mid and small-caps performing better than the main indices. The market closed with the Sensex at 75,200.85 and the Nifty 50 at 23,618.

stories.headline: Securities Fraud Investigation Into Armstrong World Industries, Inc. (AWI) Announced - Shareholders Who Lost Money Urged to Contact The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz
stories.summary: A securities fraud investigation into Armstrong World Industries, Inc. (AWI) has been announced. The investigation is focused on potential wrongdoing by the company, which may have resulted in financial losses for shareholders. Shareholders who have lost money are being urged to contact The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz for potential legal action. The investigation is ongoing, and details of the alleged wrongdoing have not been disclosed. AWI is a publicly traded company, and the investigation may impact its stock price and reputation. Shareholders who have suffered losses are advised to seek legal counsel to explore their options and potentially recover their losses. The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz is encouraging affected shareholders to come forward and seek representation.

stories.headline: New data boosts our confidence in Lilly's obesity pill. Plus, Google's new AI
stories.summary: Eli Lilly's experimental weight-loss pill, orforglipron, has shown promising results in a phase III trial, meeting weight-loss and A1C goals. The new clinical trial data has boosted confidence in the pill, lifting shares nearly 6%. This development comes as Lilly's recently approved weight-loss pill, Foundayo, saw 7,335 prescriptions in the US in its fourth week, a modest uptake compared to rival Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill. With complete weight loss data in hand, Lilly is planning regulatory filings for orforglipron and expects approvals to start arriving next year. The positive trial results have revived investor confidence in Lilly's obesity pill, positioning it for potential future success in the weight-loss market. The company's shares responded positively to the news, indicating a promising outlook for orforglipron.

stories.headline: Tony Alexander: This is not the GFC all over again - four reasons we will get that upturn
stories.summary: Independent economist Tony Alexander believes the current economic situation is not a repeat of the 2008 Global Financial Crisis (GFC). He cites four reasons for an impending upturn, despite concerns over geopolitical tensions, trade wars, and cost-of-living pressures. Alexander notes that the housing market is weaker than expected, with four consecutive house price drops. However, he suggests that factors such as Baby Boomers and a brain drain will shape demand and supply in 2025. Alexander's analysis is assisted by his five-monthly surveys, which provide insight into New Zealand's economics and housing market. He also mentions that the potential war with Iran may only delay the recovery, rather than cancel it, indicating a level of resilience in the economy. Alexander's views offer a nuanced perspective on the current economic landscape.

stories.headline: Court adjourns FCCPC contempt proceedings to May 22 Justice Ambrose-Lewis Allagoa of the Federal High Court, Lagos has adjourned to May 22, 2026, for hearing of committal proceedings filed
stories.summary: The Federal High Court in Lagos has adjourned to May 22, 2026, for the hearing of committal proceedings filed against the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC). Justice Ambrose-Lewis Allagoa made the adjournment after hearing arguments from lawyers representing the Wireless Application Service Providers Association of Nigeria (WASPAN) and the FCCPC. The contempt proceedings were initiated due to the FCCPC's alleged breach of a court order related to digital lending regulations. The court will continue hearing the matter on May 22, 2026, to determine whether the FCCPC is in contempt of court for allegedly violating the order. The FCCPC is facing contempt proceedings for its alleged non-compliance with the court's directive on digital lending. The adjournment allows for further arguments and consideration of the case.

stories.headline: Google debuts new AI models, personal AI agents in effort to keep pace with OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.summary: Google has unveiled new AI models and personal AI agents at its annual I/O developer conference. The latest version of Gemini, Gemini 3.5, is being rolled out to billions of global users, starting with Gemini 3.5 Flash, which focuses on speed. Google claims 3.5 Flash is its strongest agentic and coding model yet. The company is also introducing a new AI model designed to simulate the physical world. These announcements aim to help Google keep pace with competitors OpenAI and Anthropic, which are gearing up for IPOs. The new AI models and agents are part of Google's effort to reclaim its position as a leader in artificial intelligence and provide more advanced services to its users. The announcements were made at a time when the market is focused on the rising valuations of OpenAI and Anthropic.

stories.headline: With a backlash growing, politicians from the White House to the Capitol pivot to AI regulation
stories.summary: The White House is softening its stance on AI regulation amid a growing public backlash against the technology. Previously working to block AI regulation, the administration is now laying out a framework for national rules on artificial intelligence. The goal is to shape regulations without curbing growth in the sector. This shift comes as House Republicans and the White House push for federal control over AI regulation, echoing a similar attempt over the summer. However, key Democrats are increasingly skeptical of the White House's efforts to block state AI rules, making a national AI law unlikely in the current Congress. The new framework aims to find a balance between regulating AI and allowing the industry to continue growing. The White House's change in stance reflects the mounting pressure to address concerns surrounding AI.

stories.headline: Anthropic Just Landed One Of AI's Biggest Names
stories.summary: Andrej Karpathy, a founding member of OpenAI and former Tesla AI director, has joined Anthropic. Karpathy, known for coining the term "vibe coding," is a prominent figure in the AI community. The announcement came as Anthropic faced a federal appeals court over its designation as a "supply-chain risk" by the Defense Department. This label was given after Anthropic refused to compromise on its stance against mass surveillance and autonomous weapons. Meanwhile, Anthropic has secured $13 billion in new funding, increasing its valuation to $183 billion, triple its value six months ago. This significant investment brings Anthropic closer to its rival OpenAI, marking a substantial development in the AI industry. The funding round is one of the largest in tech history, solidifying Anthropic's position as a major player in the field.

stories.headline: OpenAI avoided a costly court loss to Elon Musk, but neither side is unscathed
stories.summary: OpenAI has prevailed in its court fight with Elon Musk, avoiding a costly loss. The company, valued at $852 billion, remains on track for a potentially record-breaking initial public offering (IPO). OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, had been engaged in a legal dispute with Musk, but the outcome has allowed the company to move forward with its plans. The IPO, which could be one of the largest in history, is still expected to proceed as planned. Despite the legal victory, neither OpenAI nor Musk has emerged unscathed from the dispute. The details of the court fight and its resolution have not been fully disclosed, but the outcome has cleared the way for OpenAI's highly anticipated IPO. The company's valuation and plans for the public offering remain unchanged following the court decision.
